title: Routing simulator and acceptance-curve driven fallback policy for speculative decoding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a routing simulator and acceptance-curve driven fallback policy to safely enable speculative decoding across heterogeneous kernels and model variants. This ticket covers the simulator, acceptance metric design, graduated fallback windows, telemetry hooks, and an experiment plan to validate production safety and cost/latency trade-offs.
background: We currently have prototype code paths for speculative decode but lack a rigorous way to quantify acceptance behavior across varying kernels (FP16, 4-bit quantized), attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling. Prior tickets implemented routing heuristics and staged fallbacks, but we need a reproducible simulator and an operationalized acceptance curve to avoid regressions and to tune graceful degradation thresholds.
proposal: 1) Implement an offline routing simulator that can replay real request traces and model prefill/decode interactions across kernel profiles and model variants. 2) Define acceptance metrics (e.g., token-level acceptance probability, prefix agreement, log-prob delta thresholds) and produce acceptance curves per model+kernel. 3) Implement a fallback policy that uses acceptance curves to select grace windows and fallback confidence thresholds at runtime. 4) Add telemetry and dashboards for continuous monitoring and automatic rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay 7 days of prod traces in <6 hours on a 4-GPU worker cluster and generate per-request routing decisions and outcome labels

Acceptance curves generated for at least 3 model families (open-llama-3b, longform-7b, mix-quant-13b) and 4 kernel profiles (native fp16, openq4, awq-4, optimized-attn) with clear per-token acceptance thresholds
Runtime fallback policy implemented behind feature flag; can be toggled per-customer and per-route
No user-visible regression in prefix-level correctness (measured by BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) beyond 1.5% on evaluation prompt set when speculative decoding is enabled
Dashboards show acceptance-rate, failover-rate, P95 latency delta, and cost-per-token delta; alerts fire when failover-rate exceeds configured threshold
End-to-end CI test validates simulator outputs against a small golden trace and a smoke test verifies fallback behaviour on next-deploy
implementation_notes: Simulator: replay engine reads anonymized request traces from S3 and replays prefill + decode steps, simulating KV cache hits/misses and batching effects. Use a modular kernel interface so new kernel profiles can be plugged in. Acceptance metrics: compute per-token log-prob delta between optimistic and conservative decodes, prefix agreement percentage, and an empirical acceptance probability curve vs token position. Fallback policy: each route holds a small table of (token-position -> acceptance-threshold) derived from the curves; at runtime the speculative router evaluates the confidence score and either commit speculative token or queue fallback decode to conservative path. Introduce a short grace window (configurable 1-5 steps) to allow optimistic tokens to be replaced without external error. Telemetry: emit event for each speculative decision with fields: model, kernel, route, token_pos, confidence, accepted (bool), fallback_trigger (reason).
tradeoffs: Aggressive acceptance thresholds increase throughput and lower cost but risk semantic regressions in generated output
Longer grace windows reduce user-visible flicker but increase latency for final commit path and complicate KV cache management
Simulator accuracy depends on quality of replayed traces and fidelity of kernel-cost models; overfitting to traces risks missing rare production edge cases
risks: Regression in output quality for safety-sensitive routes if acceptance thresholds are mis-tuned
Increased complexity in KV cache invalidation when speculative tokens are rolled back
Operational burden from new telemetry volume and false-positive rollback alerts
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for routing-simulator deterministic components. 2) Integration test to run simulator against golden trace and validate acceptance curve shape. 3) Canary rollout to internal beta orgs with feature-flag and strict alerting. 4) A/B experiment comparing standard decode vs speculative with acceptance-curve policy measuring latency P50/P95, cost-per-token, and quality regressions on held-out prompts. 5) Synthetic adversarial prompts to stress attention-window edge cases.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Merge behind feature flag and run offline at full trace scale for 48 hours. Stage 2: Enable speculative path for 5 internal customers at low traffic, monitor dashboards and SLOs for 72 hours. Stage 3: Ramp to 20% of traffic for eligible routes with automatic rollback if failover-rate > 0.5% or quality regression > 1.5%. Stage 4: Full rollout for non-sensitive routes after 2 weeks of stable metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: SpecDec/acceptance-rate, SpecDec/fallback-rate, SpecDec/p95-latency-delta, SpecDec/cost-delta, SpecDec/quality-regression. Alerts: fallback-rate > 0.5% sustained for 10 minutes, p95-latency-delta > 200ms for 5 minutes, quality-regression > 1.5% on eval probes. Create a PagerDuty escalation for high-severity alerts.
